description: Aegra migration stages 0-1: isolate Orchestra's alembic version table so Aegra's chain can share the database, triage issues that the migration supersedes, and stand up a no-traffic Aegra sidecar on :2026 against a restored copy database. Full spec in prd.md; stages 2-7 get their own issues.

userStories.title: Isolate Orchestra's alembic version table
userStories.description: As an operator, I want Orchestra's migration chain to use its own version table so Aegra's chain can coexist in the same database without a boot failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Add version_table="orchestra_alembic_version" to the offline context.configure(...) call in backend/migrations/env.py:85
Add version_table="orchestra_alembic_version" to the online context.configure(...) call in backend/migrations/env.py:102
Document the one-time 'ALTER TABLE alembic_version RENAME TO orchestra_alembic_version;' as a runbook step in the PR body, NOT as an alembic revision (it must run outside either chain)
make migrate.up followed by make migrate.down both complete cleanly against a restored dump
SELECT * FROM orchestra_alembic_version returns the current head after upgrade
backend/src/utils/migrations.py run_migrations() is not left auto-migrating in the same process Aegra will migrate in; state the chosen approach in the PR
make lint passes
make test passes
userStories.notes: Must land before any other Aegra work. Both alembic chains currently default to the same alembic_version table and Aegra runs run_migrations_if_needed() on startup, so a shared database is a boot failure rather than a manual one.

userStories.title: Triage issues the migration supersedes
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the issue queue to reflect what this migration deletes, so nobody spends effort fixing code that is scheduled for removal.
acceptanceCriteria: Comment on #974 stating it is superseded by the Aegra migration because services/schedule.py is deleted in a later stage; link this PR
Comment on #959 with the same rationale and link
Label or close #974 and #959 per the comment
Confirm the five frontend issues (#971, #970, #969, #967, #960) touch no file in the migration's deletion list, and leave them open
Do not create any new GitHub issue without explicit operator authorization
make lint passes
userStories.notes: Bookkeeping only, no code change. #951 (notebook conflict markers) ships as its own PR and must not be entangled with this one.

userStories.title: Stand up an Aegra sidecar against a copy database
userStories.description: As a developer, I want Aegra running beside the live stack against a restored copy of the database, so every subsequent stage can be validated without risking production data.
acceptanceCriteria: Create lg_template_aegra via pg_dump/pg_restore from lg_template_dev
Add a new additive file infra/docker-compose.aegra.yml running aegra-api on :2026 against lg_template_aegra
Do not modify infra/docker-compose.yml
Add a minimal aegra.json registering a hello-world graph
aegra.json store.index matches backend/src/services/db.py:82-83 exactly for dims, embed, and fields
Add make dev.aegra.up and make dev.aegra.down targets
GET localhost:2026/health returns {"status": "healthy"}
Aegra's alembic chain applies cleanly to the copy database
SELECT count(*) FROM checkpoints on the copy is unchanged from the dump
Pre-existing Orchestra store rows are readable through the sidecar's store
Run the sidecar in a named tmux window, not in an agent foreground session
Do not bind :5173 or :8000 — the primary checkout runs the operator's dev stack on those ports
make lint passes
userStories.notes: No traffic is routed to the sidecar. A dims or embed mismatch in store.index silently degrades semantic search to garbage rather than erroring, so assert it rather than eyeballing it.
